messages:
Ana: quick note — EU warm-pool saw a flurry of evictions during rmq failover overnight, approx 30% of GPU banks evicted over a ~5m window
Kevin: noticed a big bump in request_queue_length, peaked ~11.7k for eu-gpu-warm, autoscaler lagged behind by ~2.5m
Mike: I pulled logs, eviction events line up with RMQ leader churn and subsequent spike in short-lived spikes. Grafana panel `eu-warm/queue_vs_headroom` shows headroom collapsing then recovering in a sawtooth (short pulses)
Ana: current headroom alert uses `last_over_time` on a 30s scrape which is causing lots of flapping on those sub-minute pulses
Jen: alert spam woke several pagers this morning, we should make it noisier-tolerant
Mike: propose changes:
- change alert expr to use avg_over_time for smoothing (2m)
- increase alert `for:` to 4m for production pools, 2m for canaries
- add a 95p queue-duration overlay panel to correlate latency vs headroom
Kevin: also add a histogram_quantile smoothing for request latency: `histogram_quantile(0.95, sum(rate(request_duration_seconds_bucket[5m])) by (le, pool))`
Ana: sample prom query I used for percent headroom by zone:
```promql
(sum(gpu_free_slots{pool="eu-gpu-warm"}) by (zone) / sum(gpu_pool_capacity{pool="eu-gpu-warm"}) by (zone)) * 100
```
Mike: for evictions, cross-check `rate(gpu_eviction_total{pool="eu-gpu-warm"}[5m])` and `increase(eviction_total[5m])` to see short bursts
Jen: autoscaler config: warm pools have scale-up cooldown 3m and scale-down 10m. During failovers the 3m cooldown is too slow to re-warm transient capacity
Kevin: suggestion: conditional cooldowns — if `opsbot.region_failover == 1` drop scale-up cooldown to 45s for warm pools; otherwise keep 3m
ops-bot: region_failover flag currently `0` — can be toggled via `ops/region-switch` runbook
Mike: concern: aggressive cooldowns can burn burst credits and inflate billing, need cost analysis
Jen: I'll own a brief cost impact estimate if we shorten cooldowns temporarily during failovers
Ana: for alert rule debounce, here's a proposed snippet for the prom-rule PR:
```yaml
expr: avg_over_time((sum(gpu_free_slots{pool=~"eu-gpu-.*"}) / sum(gpu_pool_capacity{pool=~"eu-gpu-.*"}))[2m:30s]) * 100 < 12
for: 4m
```
Kevin: can we also add an annotation pointing to runbook `runbooks/eu-rmq-failover.md` and the dashboard panel id? makes oncall faster
Mike: batching observed behavior: batch_size_avg rose from ~7.5 -> 12.3 during the spike which held GPUs busy longer and increased tail latency
Ana: checklist:
1) update `GPU_BANK_HEADROOM` prom rule to avg_over_time + for window per pool tier
2) add derived Grafana panel: `avg batch_size` vs `headroom` with 95p latency overlay
3) create a synthetic workload in staging to reproduce failover characteristics (bursty+steady mix)
4) run cost analysis on cooldown reduction during failovers
Jen: scheduling a 30m sync tomorrow 08:30 UTC to review PRs and the cost estimates
Mike: I'll open prom-rule PR and link dashboard draft, tagging reviewers
Ana: PRs: dashboard -> https://git.redwood/s/PR/512, prom-rule -> https://git.redwood/s/PR/513
deploy-bot: applied autoscaler patch `hotfix/eu-warm-cooldown` to staging at 2026-03-17T07:10:02Z
sre-bot: alert `GPU_BANK_HEADROOM` currently firing in 3 zones (eu-west-1a,b,c) — suppressed temporarily by `for: 1m`
Kevin: please don't change prod cooldown until we validate staging behaviour and cost impact :+1:
Ana: opening ticket INF-901 with the checklist and links to PRs
ops-bot: ticket INF-901 created by Ana
Jen: thanks all, I'll prep the cost brief and we can decide in the sync
Mike: I'll run a kjob in staging that simulates rmq failover traffic pattern and post the results here
Ana: closing loop for now, keep notes in INF-901 and link any follow-ups to the dashboard PR
